init.description: Choose installations, what Home Assistant mirrors into IoT Open and what it imports. This instance: id {instance_id}.

data.export_label: Label that selects what is mirrored

data_description.add_new_installations: New installations are looked for at start-up and once an hour.
data_description.export_installation: Entities and devices with the label below are created as devices and functions in this IoT Open installation (obj/ha/… for status, set/obj/ha/… for control).
data_description.export_label: Put this label on entities or devices in Home Assistant. The label is created automatically.
data_description.export_control: Switches, lights, locks, covers, numbers, media players etc. get a topic_write (set/obj/…) that calls the Home Assistant service.
data_description.export_categorized: Off: a labelled device only mirrors its main entities, so e.g. a phone's battery and network sensors or a speaker's settings stay out of IoT Open. A label put directly on an entity is always mirrored.
data_description.export_transport: IoT Open (cloud): over the internet, needs nothing else. Local broker: over Home Assistant's MQTT integration, which must be connected to the edge client's broker in the mirror installation (for example an IoT Open Raspberry Pi). The edge client's bridge forwards values to IoT Open, and the local dashboard and Home Assistant keep talking to each other without internet. Devices and functions are still created over the internet.
data_description.instance_name: Use this value in the metadata key ha.destination on IoT Open devices or functions that should appear here (the long instance id {instance_id} also works; * means all instances).
data_description.import_mode: Only tagged: only devices/functions whose ha.destination names this instance. All: every function in the selected installations.

error.mqtt_required: Local broker needs Home Assistant's MQTT integration, connected to the edge client's broker. Add MQTT first.

export_forbidden.title: IoT Open: no permission to mirror into {installation}
export_forbidden.description:
Home Assistant cannot mirror labelled entities into the IoT Open installation **{installation}** (id {installation_id}). IoT Open answered *HTTP 403: Permission required*.

The API key or token works, but its IoT Open user is not allowed to create, change or delete devices and functions in this installation.

To fix it, either:
- give that user (or its group) a role with write access to devices and functions in the organization that owns [{installation}]({url}), or
- reconfigure the integration with an API key for a user that already has that access.

Home Assistant tries again after {retry} seconds and keeps trying until it works. This message disappears by itself when mirroring works.
